name: Osteoblast proliferation and differentiation (ALP, COL-1, OCN, Runx2)
driver: waveform / frequency structure plus cell state; B is a secondary dose scaler; dB/dt not isolated
driver_note: Non-monotonic in B and the optimum differs by lab and waveform: Yan 2015 (0.6-3.6 mT, 50 Hz) best at the lowest, 0.6 mT; Zhai 2016 (0.5-2 mT, 15.38 Hz) best at the highest, 2 mT, 2 h/day better than 6 h; Tsai 2007 sign of proliferation flips between 0.13 and 0.32 mT. Zhu 2017: 0.6 mT pulsed beat 1.8 mT sinusoid at the same 50 Hz. Jing 2014: 0.38-0.6 T rotating at 7 Hz had no effect on bone.

dBdt_Ts.basis: computed; sine/ramp assumptions in the source note; Tsai values are lower bounds because rms < peak

E_Vm.tsai_NOT_ok: the original note quoted 1.5-7.6 uV/cm, which is inconsistent with its own formula (32-160 uV/cm); do not reuse

windows.schedule: 0.5-8 h/day for days; Zhai 2 h/day best; Lohmann 8 h/day with TGF-b1 and PGE2 back to control by day 4

evidence: in vitro, many labs, cilia-dependence concentrated in two labs
confidence: moderate that an effect exists with non-monotonic dose dependence; low for numeric thresholds; speculative for B vs dB/dt
caveat: Nulls: Yang 2007 (1.55 mT, 48 Hz, MC3T3-E1), Wang 2016 (PEMF alone on hPDLSC), Diniz 2002 (inhibitory at mineralisation stage), serum, substrate and Ca-transient dependence (Pezzetti, Schwartz, Tong). 0.6 mT/50 Hz replications are the same lab.

name: Ca2+/calmodulin and adenosine A2A/A3 in bone cells
driver: unresolved; cell state (Ca transients) is a precondition
driver_note: Brighton 2001: capacitive coupling acts through voltage-gated Ca channels (verapamil), inductive and combined fields through intracellular store release (TMB-8); all converge on Ca2+/CaM (W-7). Tong 2017: effect only when Ca transients present. Kar 2021: Adora3 knockout blunts the response, Adora2A knockout only delays Alp mRNA.

windows.note: no amplitude series for these targets in the retrieved abstracts; Ferrara/IGEA 75 Hz, 1.5-2.5 mT used where stated

evidence: inhibitor and CRISPR knock-out with rescue (in vitro)
confidence: moderate-high for pathway identity; low for thresholds

name: TGF-b1, BMP-2/Smad, Wnt/b-catenin, IGF-II receptor, primary cilium
driver: frequency specificity at very low E (IGF-II); B-amplitude windows for BMP/cilia
driver_note: Fitzsimmons 1995: IGF-II receptor number rose after 30 min at 15.3 Hz combined AC/DC with calculated E_max of only 1e-5 V/m (0.1 uV/cm), frequency dependent, which argues against a Faraday E-magnitude threshold for that target. Cilia/IFT88/polaris/PC2 knockdown abolishes 0.6 mT/50 Hz and 0.5-3 mT/15 Hz effects.

windows.timing: TGF-b1 and PGE2 transient: up days 1-2, back to control at day 4 (Lohmann); PI3K peak at 0.5 h then falls (Ren 2019); DBM rat: TGF-b1 mRNA +158 %, protein +23 % (Aaron 2002)

evidence: in vitro knockdown; rat DBM in vivo; two labs for cilia
confidence: high that pathways are engaged downstream; moderate for cilia requirement; low for thresholds
caveat: Fitzsimmons B_ac of ~14 uT is a back-calculation assuming a 1.5 cm radius circular dish; the paper abstract gives neither B nor geometry.

name: Osteocyte / osteoclast / OPG-RANKL (osteoporosis)
driver: induced E level (Chang) flips sign; B windows at 15 Hz (Wang); no controlled dB/dt test
driver_note: Chang 2003 reported induced E of 4.8, 8.7, 12.2 uV/cm rms: osteoclast-like formation enhanced ~50 % or suppressed ~27 % depending on E level. Wang 2017 and 2019 at 15 Hz: 0.5 mT inhibits osteoclastogenesis and lowers RANKL/OPG, 3 mT promotes osteoclast apoptosis and resorption. Chang 2006: 3.0 uV/cm, 7.5 Hz gave apoptosis after 8 and 16 h but not 1 h.

E_Vm.basis: reported, rms uV/cm converted to V/m

windows.schedule: rat OVX 8 h/day 10 wk (Jing 2013); whole-body 12 wk (Zhou 2017); early start protected vertebra and femur, late start vertebra only

evidence: in vitro, OVX rats (n=10/group); one uncontrolled human study (Tabrah 1990, 72 Hz, n=20)
confidence: low-moderate for the 0.5 vs 3 mT window (single 15 Hz study); moderate for rat efficacy; low for humans
caveat: Jing 2013 saw no RANKL/RANK expression change while Zhou saw RANKL down and OPG up. Jing 2014 rotating 0.38-0.6 T at 7 Hz null (dB/dt 17-26 T/s is a crude geometry-dependent guess), so very large B/dB/dt is not sufficient.

name: Chondrocyte matrix synthesis / cartilage / OA
driver: frequency (75 Hz > 15 Hz in one lab) and field orientation; amplitude secondary
driver_note: Xu 2022: at 1 mT the 75 Hz condition was best (full 15/45/75 ordering not supported by the abstract; 36377077 and 36854553 are two separate papers). Stefani 2020: coil parallel to the articular surface beat perpendicular, implicating induced-E direction relative to tissue. Kavand 2019: generic PEMF null, Ca-ICR tuned AC+DC worked.

schedule.ongaro: sulfate +49 % at 7 d (grade I explants), additive with IGF-I
schedule.yang_mouse: 1 h/day for 4 wk, protection reduced in IL-6-/- and TNF-a-/-

windows.clinical: meta-analyses discordant: pain SMD 0.71 (Tong), -0.41 (Vigano), 1.06 (Yang 2020 says parameters did not matter), Chen 2019 no pain benefit; Wu 2018 reported sessions <=30 min better than >30 min (a two-bin contrast, not a dose-response curve)

evidence: in vitro, ex vivo human cartilage, mouse OA; clinical heterogeneous
confidence: moderate for anabolic effect at 1.5-3.8 mT / 75 Hz in vitro; low for frequency preference; low-moderate for clinical OA benefit

name: Tendon / fibroblast
driver_note: Only single-setting data (1.5 mT, 75 Hz, 8 h/day): collagen I/VI and scleraxis up with lower proliferation. No amplitude, frequency, E or dB/dt series.
evidence: in vitro human primary cells (13 donors); small null RCT (Ko 2024, Achilles, p=0.527); single 0.78 T bout raised pressure-pain threshold (Wilms 2024, n=34), a high-field regime unrelated to the above

name: Fracture, non-union and spinal fusion
driver: not determinable from the retrieved parameters
driver_note: Acute fracture trials are net null (Adie 2011 RR 1.02, n=259 double blind; Hannemann 2014 13 RCTs; Picelli 2024). Non-union: Cochrane 2011 union RR 1.96 (0.86-4.48), I2 58 %. Spinal fusion: Mooney 1990 92 % vs 65 % (double-blind sham), Jenis 2000 null, Foley 2007 significant at 6 months (83.6 vs 68.6 %) but not at 12; meta-analyses OR ~2.5-2.7 across stimulation types.

satter_uncontrolled.basis: computed ramp = pulse width; 11 of 13 healed in an uncontrolled series, claimed to negate a narrow window

confidence: low-moderate for non-union; low for acute fracture; moderate for spinal fusion as adjunct in high-risk cases
caveat: Satter 1999 is an uncontrolled case series of 19 enrolled / 13 completers and should not be read as efficacy evidence.
